spots.name: Lincoln Rock Light
spots.tip: Lighthouses make strong silhouettes at dusk and pair well with blue hour once the light is on.

spots.name: Manzanita Peak
spots.tip: A notable summit. Check the road and trail first; first and last light on high ground is the reason to go, and it's often the subject from below. Summit 838 m (2,749 ft).

spots.name: Sam Peak
spots.tip: A notable summit. Check the road and trail first; first and last light on high ground is the reason to go, and it's often the subject from below. Summit 737 m (2,418 ft).

spots.name: Sons of Norway Hall
spots.tip: A landmark with history. Low light brings out texture; check opening hours if it's fenced.

spots.name: Petersburg
spots.tip: eBird birding hotspot with 183 species recorded. Birds are most active in the first two hours after sunrise; recent sightings at ebird.org/hotspot/L1904567.

spots.name: Wrangell
spots.tip: eBird birding hotspot with 157 species recorded. Birds are most active in the first two hours after sunrise; recent sightings at ebird.org/hotspot/L74835554.

spots.name: Tongass/Stikine National Forest
spots.tip: Wildlife is most active in the first two hours after sunrise. Stay on trails, use your car as a blind on auto routes and give animals space.

spots.name: Wrangell: City Park
spots.tip: eBird birding hotspot with 112 species recorded. Birds are most active in the first two hours after sunrise; recent sightings at ebird.org/hotspot/L1015235.

spots.name: Whale Observatory
spots.tip: A mapped viewpoint. Check which way it faces: east for sunrise, west for sunset. Arrive 30 minutes early to scout foreground.

spots.name: Rainbow Falls
spots.tip: Best under soft overcast or in shade so the highlights don't blow out. A slow shutter (1/4–1 s on a tripod) smooths the water; flow peaks after rain and snowmelt.
